subject: Can I and how do I specify a heteroscedastic Gaussian noise in a spatial SPDE model ?

messages.author: 06bb4192c46c7b61
messages.subject: Can I and how do I specify a heteroscedastic Gaussian noise in a spatial SPDE model ?
parts:
Hi all,

I'm new to INLA so I might be asking silly questions.
I am working with a SPDE model for Gaussian data with spatial auto-correlation, with the classical formmulation

y(u) = X(u)Beta + w(u) + epsilon(u),
  • u being the coordinate of the spatial observations.
  • X() being covariates.
  • Beta being a vector of regression coefficients.
  • w() accounting for spatial auto-correlation and being a Gaussian (Markov) random field.
  • epsilon() accounting for independent errors.
Thanks to several references such as https://becarioprecario.bitbucket.io/spde-gitbook/ch-nonstationarity.html   or https://sites.google.com/a/r-inla.org/stbook/, I could figure out how to specify varying range and marginal variance for w() through the Btau and Bkappa matrices. However, I also would like to integrate covariates to explain the log-variance of epsilon() so that the resulting noise is heteroscedastic. Could someone give me a hint ?

Thank you in advance
Sébastien

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Can I and how do I specify a heteroscedastic Gaussian noise in a spatial SPDE model ?
parts:
Hi,

There are other approaches (such as inla.rgeneric), but one way is to take advantage of the internal spde model implementation, that allows you to use other matrices than those from the SPDE construction; in the inla.spde.generic function, M0, M1, and M2 would usually be c0, g1, and g2 (with some scaling factors) from inla.mesh.fem(), but you could set M0=I and M1=M2=0 to be able to build your epsilon(u) model via the tau parameter (and make kappa fixed to 1).

For the model with loglinear variance w.r.t. a covariate matrix X (note: just as for the spde models, keep the dimension ncol(X) small!)
  epsilon = N(0, diag(2 * X * beta))
the precision matrix is
  Q = T %*% M0 %*% T
where T is diagonal with logarithm X %*% beta and M0 is an identity matrix

the code should look like this (or similar; I haven't tested all the matrix details):

model <-
  inla.spde2.generic(M0 = Diagonal(n=nrow(X), x=1.0), M1 = Diagonal(n=nrow(X), x=0.0), M2 = Diagonal(n=nrow(X), x=0.0),
    B0 = cbind(0, X), B1 = matrix(0, 1, 1+ ncol(X)), B2 = matrix(0, 1, 1+ ncol(X)),
    theta.mu = rep(0,ncol(X)),
    theta.Q = diag(rep(1,ncol(X))),
    transform = "identity")

the beta priors above are all set to N(0,1) via theta.mu and theta.Q; change them to something more reasonable for your problem.

You then use it just like the spde models, but with the A matrix set to Diagonal(1.0, n)

Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Can I and how do I specify a heteroscedastic Gaussian noise in a spatial SPDE model ?
parts:
Dear Finn, 

I went on with my implementation but a few points are confusing me.

The first point is that I have about 50000 spatial observations, and using the standard mesh constructors of INLA I have a mesh with about 20000 nodes.
I understood that the B_kappa and B_tau matrices of the coherent spatial effect w(u) must have 20000 rows : each row of B_kappa, B_tau corresponds to the value of the covariates taken at the mesh nodes. Just to be sure, do the X you mentioned in your answer correspond to covariates evaluated at the mesh nodes or at the observations ? In other words, in my case, is the n you mentioned equal to 20000 or to 50000 ?

The second point is how I should combine the spatially coherent spatial effect and the heteroscedastic noise in the same model. I started from simple examples I saw in the tutorials and tinkered a solution using INLA::inla.stack() . While I have no bug when I run that (it's something !), I still have doubts about the validity of this code. Does my stack and formula construction seem sound to you ?

stk <- INLA::inla.stack(
  data = list(y = observed_field),
  A = list(A_noise,    # the Identity matrix you mentioned
                A_field,     # generated using the mesh and INLA::inla.spde.make.A()
                1               # for fixed effects
                ),
  effects=list(
    INLA::inla.spde.make.index(name = "heteroscedastic.noise", spde_noise$n.spde                        ),  #the noise index
    INLA::inla.spde.make.index(name = "spatial.field",                    spde_spatially_coherent$n.spde ),  #the spatial field index
    X_split                                                                                                                                                               #a list containing the covariates for fixed effects
  ))

formula = observed_field ~
  - 1 +                                                                                            # removing superfluous intercept as advised by INLA
  dairp + dmino + dquksig + dTRI + gcarb + globedem +    # fixed effects
  nlights03 + sdroads + twi + vsky + winde +                        # fixed effects
  f(heteroscedastic.noise, model = spde_noise)+                # heteroskedastic Gaussian noise
  f(spatial.field, model = spde_spatially_coherent)              # spatially coherent random effect


Last question, about the link function family. While I assume my data to be Gaussian, it feels redundant to fill the argument family="gaussian" in the INLA::inla() function. Indeed, the Gaussian noise is be captured by the SPDE you gave me, and once the fixed effects, the spatially coherent field, and the heteroscedastic noise are added, there is nothing left.
Therefore, it feels much more natural to me to use the control.family argument like https://becarioprecario.bitbucket.io/spde-gitbook/ch-nonstationarity.html . In their toy example, they have a noise-less data set, so they force the latent field to stick to the observed data. This is exactly what I want to do, except that I have two latent fields.
This gives me the following code, again does it look sound to you ?

clik <- list(hyper = list(prec = list(initial = 20,  fixed = TRUE))) very high precision of Gaussian observations
res <- INLA::inla(
            formula,                                                                                                                    # the aformentioned formula
            data = INLA::inla.stack.data(stk),                                                                         # the aformentioned stack
            control.family = clik,                                                                                                # control family with high precision
            control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE, A = INLA::inla.stack.A(stk)),
            verbose = T)

Once again, many many thanks for your answer !
Sébastien

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Can I and how do I specify a heteroscedastic Gaussian noise in a spatial SPDE model ?
parts:
Hi,

The heteroscedastic noise component is unrelated to the mesh, since it contributes directly to each individual observations, so the number of rows should equal the number of observations, i.e. 50000.

One thing to keep in mind is that when you construct the mesh, you don't have to use the observation points as "seed points"; in fact, doing that can cause problematic node clusters when there is a lot of locations. Instead, focus on the resolution of the mesh, so that it can capture the needed spatial scales (At least in the vicinity of data).  A practical way to do that is to increase the cutoff value, which will make it ignore many of the input points, and produce a smoother triangulation, usually with fewer triangles.

A follow-up email about the need for the control.family trick get stuck in my drafts; yes, setting the observation precision to a large value is the right way here.

Finn

The second point is how I should combine the spatially coherent spatial effect and the heteroscedastic noise in the same model. I started from simple examples I saw in the tutorials and tinkered a solution using INLA::inla.stack() . While I have no bug when I run that (it's something !), I still have doubts about the validity of this code. Does my stack and formula construction seem sound to you ?

stk <- INLA::inla.stack(
  data = list(y = observed_field),
  A = list(A_noise,    # the Identity matrix you mentioned
                A_field,     # generated using the mesh and INLA::inla.spde.make.A()
                1               # for fixed effects
                ),
  effects=list(
    INLA::inla.spde.make.index(name = "heteroscedastic.noise", spde_noise$n.spde                        ),  #the noise index
    INLA::inla.spde.make.index(name = "spatial.field",                    spde_spatially_coherent$n.spde ),  #the spatial field index
    X_split                                                                                                                                                               #a list containing the covariates for fixed effects
  ))

formula = observed_field ~
  - 1 +                                                                                            # removing superfluous intercept as advised by INLA
  dairp + dmino + dquksig + dTRI + gcarb + globedem +    # fixed effects
  nlights03 + sdroads + twi + vsky + winde +                        # fixed effects
  f(heteroscedastic.noise, model = spde_noise)+                # heteroskedastic Gaussian noise
  f(spatial.field, model = spde_spatially_coherent)              # spatially coherent random effect


Last question, about the link function family. While I assume my data to be Gaussian, it feels redundant to fill the argument family="gaussian" in the INLA::inla() function. Indeed, the Gaussian noise is be captured by the SPDE you gave me, and once the fixed effects, the spatially coherent field, and the heteroscedastic noise are added, there is nothing left.
Therefore, it feels much more natural to me to use the control.family argument like https://becarioprecario.bitbucket.io/spde-gitbook/ch-nonstationarity.html . In their toy example, they have a noise-less data set, so they force the latent field to stick to the observed data. This is exactly what I want to do, except that I have two latent fields.
This gives me the following code, again does it look sound to you ?

clik <- list(hyper = list(prec = list(initial = 20,  fixed = TRUE))) very high precision of Gaussian observations
res <- INLA::inla(
            formula,                                                                                                                    # the aformentioned formula
            data = INLA::inla.stack.data(stk),                                                                         # the aformentioned stack
            control.family = clik,                                                                                                # control family with high precision
            control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE, A = INLA::inla.stack.A(stk)),
            verbose = T)

Once again, many many thanks for your answer !
Sébastien

The code ran well. Thank you all for this great technical support, this was really really helpful.

Here is my code in case someone wants to scrap some pieces of it.  I used a homemade package Bidart and reprocessed data from https://spatial-analyst.net/book/NGS8HMC , nonetheless some parts may come in handy.
Before you run the code make sure that :
  • R version is up to date (in R 3.6 the RAM cost was much higher)
  • the computer has plenty of RAM if you are using several cores (I had to set up a 100 G swap file)
  • as said by Håvard the number of parameters is lower than 52, else be using empirical Bayes


#############
# load data #
#############

train_data_set = readRDS("Heavy_metals_comparison/validation_train.RDS")
coords = train_data_set$train_locs

#################
# get inla mesh #
#################

lonlat_CRS = sp::CRS("+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84 +no_defs +ellps=WGS84 +towgs84=0,0,0")
prdomain <- INLA::inla.nonconvex.hull(points = coords, convex = -0.03, concave = -0.05,
                                  resolution=c(100,100), crs = lonlat_CRS)
prmesh <- INLA::inla.mesh.2d(boundary=prdomain, max.edge=c(.45,1),
                         cutoff=0.2, crs = lonlat_CRS)
warnings()
# I get waring whrn I put crs
plot(prmesh$loc, pch = 16, cex = .1)

###################################################
# get environmental covariates at INLA mesh nodes #
###################################################

# loqd environmental covariates
load(file = "Heavy_metals/NGS8HMC.Rdata")
grid.list <- c("dairp.asc", "dmino.asc", "dquksig.asc", "dTRI.asc", "gcarb.asc",
               "geomap.asc", "globedem.asc", "minotype.asc", "nlights03.asc", "sdroads.asc",
               "twi.asc", "vsky.asc", "winde.asc", "glwd31.asc")
gridmaps <- rgdal::readGDAL("Heavy_metals/usgrids5km/dairp.asc")
names(gridmaps)[1] <- sub(".asc", "", grid.list[1])
for(i in grid.list[-1]) {
  gridmaps@data[sub(".asc", "", i[1])] <- rgdal::readGDAL(paste("Heavy_metals/usgrids5km/",i, sep = ""))$band1
}
# projection of environmental covariates
AEA <- "+proj=aea +lat_1=29.5 +lat_2=45.5 +lat_0=23 +lon_0=-96 +x_0=0 +y_0=0
+ellps=GRS80 +datum=NAD83 +units=m +no_defs"
sp::proj4string(gridmaps) = sp::CRS(AEA)

# put INLA nodes in same CRS as environmental covariates
INLA_locs = data.frame(prmesh$loc[,-3])
INLA_nodes_data <- sp::SpatialPointsDataFrame(coords = INLA_locs[,c(1, 2)], data = INLA_locs,
                               proj4string = lonlat_CRS)
INLA_nodes_data_AEA = sp::spTransform(INLA_nodes_data, AEA)

# overlay environemntal covariates grid on INLA nodes
X_locs_INLA = sp::over(INLA_nodes_data_AEA, gridmaps)

###############################
# imputation of missing nodes #
###############################

par(mfrow = c(2, 1))


Bidart::plot_pointillist_painting(
  INLA_locs[!is.na(X_locs_INLA$twi),c(1,2)],
  X_locs_INLA$twi[!is.na(X_locs_INLA$twi)],
  main = "observed and unobserved twi"
)
points(INLA_locs[is.na(X_locs_INLA$twi),c(1,2)], pch = 16)
maps::map("state", add = T)

X_locs_INLA$twi[is.na(X_locs_INLA$twi)] = mean(X_locs_INLA$twi, na.rm = T)
Bidart::plot_pointillist_painting(
  INLA_locs,
  X_locs_INLA$twi,
  main = "observed and imputed twi"
)
points(INLA_locs[is.na(X_locs_INLA$twi),c(1,2)], pch = 16)
maps::map("state", add = T)


Bidart::plot_pointillist_painting(
  INLA_locs[!is.na(X_locs_INLA$gcarb),c(1,2)],
  X_locs_INLA$gcarb[!is.na(X_locs_INLA$gcarb)],
  main = "observed and unobserved gcarb"
)
points(INLA_locs[is.na(X_locs_INLA$gcarb),c(1,2)], pch = 16)
maps::map("state", add = T)

X_locs_INLA$gcarb[is.na(X_locs_INLA$gcarb)] = mean(X_locs_INLA$gcarb, na.rm = T)
Bidart::plot_pointillist_painting(
  INLA_locs,
  X_locs_INLA$gcarb,
  main = "observed and imputed gcarb"
)
maps::map("state", add = T)

X_locs_INLA$globedem = X_locs_INLA$globedem * (X_locs_INLA$globedem>0)
Bidart::plot_pointillist_painting(
  INLA_locs[!is.na(X_locs_INLA$globedem),c(1,2)],
  X_locs_INLA$globedem[!is.na(X_locs_INLA$globedem)],
  main = "observed and unobserved globedem"
)
points(INLA_locs[is.na(X_locs_INLA$globedem),c(1,2)], pch = 16)
maps::map("state", add = T)

X_locs_INLA$globedem[is.na(X_locs_INLA$globedem)] = 0
Bidart::plot_pointillist_painting(
  INLA_locs,
  X_locs_INLA$globedem,
  main = "observed and imputed globedem"
)
maps::map("state", add = T)

# creating evironmental covariates vector
X_range_env_INLA = do.call(cbind, list(X_locs_INLA$globedem, X_locs_INLA$twi, X_locs_INLA$gcarb))

#####################
# scaling INLA data #
#####################
apply(X_range_env_INLA, 2, mean)
apply(X_range_env_INLA, 2, sd)

processed_data = readRDS("Heavy_metals_comparison/processed_data.RDS")
X_range_env_INLA = X_range_env_INLA - tcrossprod(rep(1, nrow(X_range_env_INLA)), processed_data$X_locs_mean[c("globedem", "twi", "gcarb")])
X_range_env_INLA = X_range_env_INLA %*% diag(1/processed_data$X_locs_sd[c("globedem", "twi", "gcarb")])
apply(X_range_env_INLA, 2, mean)
apply(X_range_env_INLA, 2, sd)

#######################
# precicting KL basis #
#######################

KL_basis_for_INLA = Bidart::predict_KL_basis(
  KL_basis = train_data_set$train_KL_decomposition,
  predicted_locs = prmesh$loc[,c(1,2)],
  seed =1)
dev.off()
par(mfrow = c(2,2))
Bidart::plot_pointillist_painting(prmesh$loc[,c(1,2)], KL_basis_for_INLA[,1])
maps::map("state", add = T)
Bidart::plot_pointillist_painting(prmesh$loc[,c(1,2)], KL_basis_for_INLA[,2])
maps::map("state", add = T)
Bidart::plot_pointillist_painting(prmesh$loc[,c(1,2)], KL_basis_for_INLA[,3])
maps::map("state", add = T)
Bidart::plot_pointillist_painting(prmesh$loc[,c(1,2)], KL_basis_for_INLA[,4])
maps::map("state", add = T)

#############################
# making A matrix and SPDEs #
#############################

n_spatial_basis = 25 # number of spatial basis function covariates
# that will go into the SPDEs

  ##########################################
  # nonsationary spatially coherent effect #
  ##########################################
A_field = INLA::inla.spde.make.A(prmesh, # SPDE mesh
                                 loc=coords # coordinates of the observations of the interest variable
                                 )
# A_field has as many rows as observations of the interest variable,
# and as many columns as the number of nodes in the SPDE mesh
X_kappa_tau = (do.call(cbind, list(1, as.matrix(KL_basis_for_INLA[,seq(n_spatial_basis)]), X_range_env_INLA)))
# X_kappa_tau corresponds to observations of the covariates ***at the mesh nodes***
colnames(X_kappa_tau) =
  c("intercept", as.character(seq(n_spatial_basis)), c("globedem", "twi", "gcarb"))
spde_spatially_coherent = INLA::inla.spde2.matern(mesh = prmesh, alpha=2,
                                B.tau = cbind(1, X_kappa_tau), # regressors for range and marginal variance
                                B.kappa = cbind(1, X_kappa_tau), # regressors for range
                                )

  ########################################
  # stationary spatially coherent effect #
  ########################################
## A_field = INLA::inla.spde.make.A(prmesh, # SPDE mesh
##                                  loc=coords # coordinates of the observations of the interest variable
##                                  )
## # A_field has as many rows as observations of the interest variable,
## # and as many columns as the number of nodes in the SPDE mesh
## X_kappa_tau = (do.call(cbind, list(1, as.matrix(KL_basis_for_INLA[,seq(n_spatial_basis)]), X_range_env_INLA)))
## # X_kappa_tau corresponds to observations of the covariates ***at the mesh nodes***
## colnames(X_kappa_tau) =
##   c("intercept", as.character(seq(n_spatial_basis)), c("globedem", "twi", "gcarb"))
## spde_spatially_coherent = INLA::inla.spde2.matern(mesh = prmesh, alpha=2
##                                 )

  #######################################
  # nonstationary heteroscedastic noise #
  #######################################
 X_noise = as.matrix(cbind(
   train_data_set$train_KL_decomposition$basis[,seq(n_spatial_basis)],
   train_data_set$train_X))
 # X_noise corresponds to observations of the covariates
 # ***at the coordinates of the observations***
 A_noise = Matrix::Diagonal(n=nrow(X_noise), x=1)
 # A noise is an identity matrix with
 # as many rows and columns as the number of observations
 spde_noise <- INLA::inla.spde2.generic(
   M0 = Matrix::Diagonal(n=nrow(X_noise), x=1.0),
   M1 = Matrix::Diagonal(n=nrow(X_noise), x=0.0),
   M2 = Matrix::Diagonal(n=nrow(X_noise), x=0.0),
   B0 = cbind(0, X_noise), B1 = matrix(0, 1, 1+ ncol(X_noise)),
   B2 = matrix(0, 1, 1+ ncol(X_noise)),
   theta.mu = rep(0,ncol(X_noise)),
   theta.Q = diag(rep(.00001,ncol(X_noise))), # very weak prior
   transform = "identity")  


#############################
# prepare stack and formula #
#############################

observed_field = train_data_set$train_field # interest variable
X = train_data_set$train_X # covariates
X_split = list()
for(name in colnames(X))X_split[[name]] = X[,name]

  ##################################
  # spatially coherent effect only #
  ##################################
##
##stk <- INLA::inla.stack(
##  data = list(y = observed_field),
##  A = list(A_field,1),
##  effects=list(
##    c(list(Intercept=1), #the Intercept
##      INLA::inla.spde.make.index(
##        name = "spatial.field",
##        spde_spatially_coherent$n.spde)),  #the spatial field index
##        # the length of the spatial index is equal to the number of mesh nodes
##    X_split #the covariates
##  ))
##
##formula = observed_field ~
##  - 1 + # removing superfluous intercept as advised by INLA
##  dairp + dmino + dquksig + dTRI + gcarb + globedem +
##  nlights03 + sdroads + twi + vsky + winde + # fixed effects
##  f(spatial.field, model = spde_spatially_coherent) # spatially coherent random effect



  ###############################
  # heterosceddastic noise only #
  ###############################

##stk <- INLA::inla.stack(
##  data = list(y = observed_field),
##  A = list(A_noise,1),
##  effects=list(
##    c(list(Intercept=1), #the Intercept
##      INLA::inla.spde.make.index(
##        name = "heteroscedastic.noise",
##        spde_noise$n.spde)), #the noise index
##    # the length of the noise index is equal to the number of observations
##    X_split #the covariates
##  ))
##
##formula = observed_field ~
##  - 1 + # removing superfluous intercept as advised by INLA
##  dairp + dmino + dquksig + dTRI + gcarb + globedem +
##  nlights03 + sdroads + twi + vsky + winde + # fixed effects
##  f(heteroscedastic.noise, model = spde_noise)  # heteroskedastic Gaussian noise

  #################################################
  # combining noise and spatially coherent effect #
  #################################################

stk <- INLA::inla.stack(
  data = list(y = observed_field),

A = list(A_noise, A_field, 1),
  effects=list(
    INLA::inla.spde.make.index(
      name = "heteroscedastic.noise",
      spde_noise$n.spde), #the noise index
    # the length of the noise index is equal to the number of observations
    INLA::inla.spde.make.index(
      name = "spatial.field",
      spde_spatially_coherent$n.spde),  #the spatial field index
    # the length of the spatial index is equal to the number of mesh nodes
    X_split #the covariates

))

formula = observed_field ~
  - 1 + # removing superfluous intercept as advised by INLA
  dairp + dmino + dquksig + dTRI + gcarb + globedem +

nlights03 + sdroads + twi + vsky + winde + # fixed effects
  f(heteroscedastic.noise, model = spde_noise)+ # heteroskedastic Gaussian noise
  f(spatial.field, model = spde_spatially_coherent) # spatially coherent random effect

#######
# run #
#######

  #################################
  # run  with nonstationary noise #
  #################################

##clik <- list(hyper = list(prec = list(initial = 20,
##                                      fixed = TRUE)))
##res <- INLA::inla(formula, data = INLA::inla.stack.data(stk), control.family = clik,
##             control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE, A = INLA::inla.stack.A(stk)), verbose = T)
##saveRDS(res, "Heavy_metals_comparison/res_INLA.RDS")

  #####################################################################################################
  # run  with nonstationary noise and latent field, with empirical Bayes bc of limit number of params #
  #####################################################################################################

clik <- list(hyper = list(prec = list(initial = 20,
                                      fixed = TRUE)))
res <- INLA::inla(formula, data = INLA::inla.stack.data(stk), control.family = clik, control.inla=list(int.strategy="eb"),
control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE, A = INLA::inla.stack.A(stk)), verbose = T)

saveRDS(res, "Heavy_metals_comparison/res_INLA.RDS")

  #######################################################################
  # run with stationary noise, either with stat or nonstat latent field #
  #######################################################################


##res <- INLA::inla(formula, data = INLA::inla.stack.data(stk), family = "gaussian",
##             control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE, A = INLA::inla.stack.A(stk)), verbose = T)
